theory.intro: When two chords, two secants, or a tangent and a secant intersect (either inside or outside a circle), the products of their intercepts are related by fixed rules. These let you find an unknown length once the others are known.
facts: Two chords $AB$ and $CD$ intersecting inside a circle at $P$ satisfy $AP \times PB = CP \times PD$.

Two secants from an external point $P$, meeting the circle at $A, B$ and $C, D$ respectively (with $A, C$ the nearer points), satisfy $PA \times PB = PC \times PD$, using the full distance from $P$ to each point.
A tangent $PC$ and a secant from the same external point $P$, meeting the circle at $N$ (near) and $F$ (far), satisfy $PC^{2} = PN \times PF$.
steps: Identify which rule applies: two chords crossing inside the circle, two secants from an external point, or a tangent and secant from an external point.
Write the product-of-intercepts equation using the full lengths from the point of intersection.
Substitute the known lengths and solve for the unknown.

foundation.solution_text:
$AP \times PB = CP \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting chords are equal)
$8 \times 3 = 6 \times PD$
$24 = 6 \times PD$
$PD = 4\text{ cm}$

$PA \times PB = PC \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting secants are equal)
$4 \times 9 = 3 \times PD$
$36 = 3 \times PD$
$PD = 12\text{ cm}$

$PC^{2} = PN \times PF$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$6^{2} = 4 \times PF$
$36 = 4 \times PF$
$PF = 9\text{ cm}$

$PC^{2} = PN \times PF$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$8^{2} = 4 \times PF$
$64 = 4 \times PF$
$PF = 16\text{ cm}$
$NF = PF - PN = 16 - 4 = 12\text{ cm}$

$AP \times PB = CP \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting chords are equal)
$x(x + 2) = 5 \times 3$
$x^{2} + 2x = 15$
$x^{2} + 2x - 15 = 0$
$(x + 5)(x - 3) = 0$
$x = 3$ (rejecting the negative length $x = -5$)
$PC^{2} = PN \times PF$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)

development.solution_text:
$PA \times PB = PC \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting secants are equal)
$x(x + 7) = 6 \times 10$
$x^{2} + 7x - 60 = 0$
$(x + 12)(x - 5) = 0$
$x = 5$ (rejecting the negative length $x = -12$)

$PC^{2} = PN \times PF$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$10^{2} = PN \times 25$
$100 = 25 \times PN$
$PN = 4\text{ cm}$
$NF = PF - PN = 25 - 4 = 21\text{ cm}$

$PA \times PB = PC \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting secants are equal)
$6 \times 9 = x(x + 15)$
$x^{2} + 15x - 54 = 0$
$(x + 18)(x - 3) = 0$
$x = 3$ (rejecting the negative length $x = -18$)

$PA \times PB = PC \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting secants are equal)
$6 \times 14 = 7 \times PD$
$84 = 7 \times PD$
$PD = 12\text{ km}$

$AP \times PB = CP \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting chords are equal)
$x(x + 3) = 5 \times 9$
$x^{2} + 3x - 45 = 0$

$PA \times PB = PC \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting secants are equal)
$4 \times PB = 5 \times 20$
$4 \times PB = 100$
$PB = 25\text{ cm}$
$AB = PB - PA = 25 - 4 = 21\text{ cm}$
$CD = PD - PC = 20 - 5 = 15\text{ cm}$

mastery.solution_text:
In $\triangle APD$ and $\triangle CPB$:
$\angle DAP = \angle BCP$ (angles subtended at the circumference by chord $DB$ are equal)
$\angle ADP = \angle CBP$ (angles subtended at the circumference by chord $AC$ are equal)
$\therefore \triangle APD \sim \triangle CPB$ (equiangular)
$\frac{AP}{CP} = \frac{PD}{PB}$ (corresponding sides of similar triangles are in proportion)
$AP \times PB = CP \times PD$ (cross-multiplying)

$AP \times PB = CP \times PD$ (products of intercepts of intersecting chords are equal)
Since $AP = DP$, this gives $PB = CP$
$AB = AP + PB$ and $DC = DP + CP$
Since $AP = DP$ and $PB = CP$, adding gives $AP + PB = DP + CP$
$\therefore AB = DC$

(a) The line through $P$, $N$ and the far point of the surface is a secant through the centre $O$, so its near intercept is $PN = h$ and its far intercept is $PN + 2R = h + 2R$
$PC^{2} = PN \times (\text{far intercept})$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$d^{2} = h(h + 2R)$
$d^{2} = h(2R + h)$
(b) $R = 6000\text{ km} = 6\,000\,000\text{ m}$
$d^{2} = 2(2 \times 6\,000\,000 + 2)$
$d^{2} = 2(12\,000\,002)$
$d^{2} = 24\,000\,004$
$d \approx 4899\text{ m}$
